topic: Endorsements, logbook entries and instructor records

notes.front: What is the pre-solo knowledge test?
notes.back: The knowledge test a student pilot must complete satisfactorily before being authorised to fly solo.
notes.explanation: It is the first gate to solo: aeronautical knowledge is shown before solo flight is authorised.
notes.example: Like the written check a new lifeguard passes before being left alone in charge of the pool.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 20.2, page 11
notes.evidence: Before being authorized to conduct a solo flight, a student pilot must have demonstrated satisfactory aeronautical knowledge by completion of a knowledge test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which regulations must the pre-solo knowledge test address?
notes.back: The applicable sections of parts 61 and 91.
notes.explanation: Part 61 holds the student's own solo rules and part 91 the general operating rules the student will fly under.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)
notes.evidence: (1) The test must address the student pilot's knowledge of— (i) Applicable sections of parts 61 and 91 of this chapter;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What local knowledge must the pre-solo knowledge test address?
notes.back: Airspace rules and procedures for the airport where the solo flight will be performed.
notes.explanation: The test is tied to the particular airport of the solo, not to airspace in general.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)
notes.evidence: (ii) Airspace rules and procedures for the airport where the solo flight will be performed; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What aircraft knowledge must the pre-solo knowledge test address?
notes.back: Flight characteristics and operational limitations of the make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: It is specific to the make and model, like the solo endorsement that follows it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)
notes.evidence: (iii) Flight characteristics and operational limitations for the make and model of aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What two duties does §61.87(b)(2) give the student's authorized instructor for the pre-solo knowledge test?
notes.back: Administer the test; review all incorrect answers with the student before authorising solo.
notes.explanation: The review of wrong answers must be complete before solo is authorised, not afterwards.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (b)(2)
notes.evidence: (2) The student's authorized instructor must— (i) Administer the test; and (ii) At the conclusion of the test, review all incorrect answers with the student before authorizing that student to conduct a solo flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A learner scores 90% on the pre-solo knowledge test. Short of time, the instructor endorses her for solo and plans to go over the two wrong answers next week. What does §61.87(b)(2) require?
notes.back: C) The incorrect answers must be reviewed with the learner before solo is authorised
notes.choices:
A) Nothing more: a high score needs no review
B) The review may be done within 90 days
C) The incorrect answers must be reviewed with the learner before solo is authorised
D) Another instructor must grade the test
notes.choicesExplained: A: the rule says all incorrect answers, whatever the score. B: the 90-day figure belongs to solo endorsements, not the review. D: the student's authorized instructor administers the test.
notes.explanation: The rule makes the review of all incorrect answers a step that comes before authorising solo.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (b)(2)
notes.evidence: (ii) At the conclusion of the test, review all incorrect answers with the student before authorizing that student to conduct a solo flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What flight training must a student have received and logged before solo?
notes.back: Training on the §61.87 manoeuvres and procedures appropriate to the make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: The manoeuvres differ by category and class, and §61.87(d) lists those for single-engine airplanes.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (c)
notes.evidence: (1) Received and logged flight training for the maneuvers and procedures of this section that are appropriate to the make and model of aircraft to be flown; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Who judges a student's pre-solo proficiency, and in what aircraft?
notes.back: An authorized instructor, in the make and model to be flown or a similar make and model.
notes.explanation: The standard is satisfactory proficiency and safety, as judged by the instructor.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (c)
notes.evidence: (2) Demonstrated satisfactory proficiency and safety, as judged by an authorized instructor, on the maneuvers and procedures required by this section in the make and model of aircraft or similar make and model of aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Ravi soloed last month in one two-seat trainer. His club now asks him to solo a quite different model he has never flown. What must happen first under §61.87(c)?
notes.back: B) He must receive and log training in that make and model and show proficiency in it (or a similar one) to an instructor
notes.choices:
A) Nothing: his solo endorsement covers any airplane
B) He must receive and log training in that make and model and show proficiency in it (or a similar one) to an instructor
C) He only needs to read that model's handbook
D) He needs a new student pilot certificate
notes.choicesExplained: A: solo endorsements are for a specific make and model. C: reading alone is not logged flight training. D: the student pilot certificate is not model-specific.
notes.explanation: Training and proficiency shown in one model do not cover a quite different model he has never flown.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (c)
notes.evidence: (2) Demonstrated satisfactory proficiency and safety, as judged by an authorized instructor, on the maneuvers and procedures required by this section in the make and model of aircraft or similar make and model of aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How recent must a student's solo endorsement be, and who gives it?
notes.back: Given within the 90 days before the flight, for the specific make and model, by an authorized instructor who gave the training.
notes.explanation: The endorsement is tied both to a model and to a time limit, so it lapses unless renewed.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (n)
notes.evidence: unless that student pilot has received an endorsement in the student's logbook for the specific make and model aircraft to be flown by an authorized instructor who gave the training within the 90 days preceding the date of the flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How does a student keep solo privileges beyond the first 90 days?
notes.back: An authorized instructor updates the student's logbook endorsement every 90 days.
notes.explanation: AC 61-65K gives separate sample endorsements for the first 90-day period and for each later one.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: that endorsement remains current for solo flight privileges, provided an authorized instructor updates the student's logbook every 90 days thereafter.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A student's solo endorsement for her training airplane is dated 1 March. On 5 June she plans a local solo in the same airplane. May she go?
notes.back: D) No: the endorsement is more than 90 days old and must be updated by an authorized instructor
notes.choices:
A) Yes: her plastic student pilot certificate does not expire
B) No: she needs a new student pilot certificate
C) Yes, if she carries her logbook
D) No: the endorsement is more than 90 days old and must be updated by an authorized instructor
notes.choicesExplained: A: the certificate does not expire, but the solo endorsement does. C: carrying the logbook does not make an old endorsement current. B: the certificate is still valid; the endorsement is the problem.
notes.explanation: From 1 March, 90 days end before June, so the endorsement no longer covers the flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (n)
notes.evidence: unless that student pilot has received an endorsement in the student's logbook for the specific make and model aircraft to be flown by an authorized instructor who gave the training within the 90 days preceding the date of the flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What night training must a student receive before solo flight at night?
notes.back: Night takeoffs, approaches, landings and go-arounds at the solo airport, and night navigation training near it.
notes.explanation: Both parts of the training are tied to the airport where the night solo will be conducted.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (o)
notes.evidence: (1) Flight training at night on night flying procedures that includes takeoffs, approaches, landings, and go-arounds at night at the airport where the solo flight will be conducted; (2) Navigation training at night in the vicinity of the airport where the solo flight will be conducted; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What endorsement does a student need for night solo?
notes.back: A night solo endorsement for the specific make and model, from an instructor who gave the training within the preceding 90 days.
notes.explanation: It is separate from the day solo endorsement, with its own 90-day limit.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (o)
notes.evidence: (3) An endorsement in the student's logbook for the specific make and model aircraft to be flown for night solo flight by an authorized instructor who gave the training within the 90-day period preceding the date of the flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Before authorising a student's solo, in what aircraft must the instructor have trained the student?
notes.back: The make and model of the solo aircraft, or a similar make and model.
notes.explanation: This limit binds the instructor, matching the student's own make-and-model rules.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: (1) Given that student pilot training in the make and model of aircraft or a similar make and model of aircraft in which the solo flight is to be flown;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor have determined about the student's manoeuvres before authorising solo?
notes.back: That the student is proficient in the manoeuvres and procedures prescribed in §61.87.
notes.explanation: The instructor's finding covers the full pre-solo list, not only takeoffs and landings.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: (2) Determined the student pilot is proficient in the maneuvers and procedures prescribed in this section;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor have determined about the student and the solo aircraft before authorising solo?
notes.back: That the student is proficient in the make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: Proficiency in the manoeuvres and proficiency in the particular aircraft are separate findings.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: (3) Determined the student pilot is proficient in the make and model of aircraft to be flown; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What logbook step completes an instructor's authorisation of solo under §61.87(p)?
notes.back: Endorsing the student's logbook for the specific make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: The endorsement then stays current only if it is updated every 90 days.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: (4) Endorsed the student pilot's logbook for the specific make and model aircraft to be flown
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: According to AC 61-65K, who must give the endorsements that authorise and limit a student's solo privileges?
notes.back: The authorized flight instructor who gave the student the training.
notes.explanation: The advisory circular bases this on §61.87(p).
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 20.1, page 11
notes.evidence: Per 14 CFR § 61.87(p), the authorized flight instructor who gave the training to the student must give these endorsements.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Mo's usual instructor is on holiday. Another instructor, who has never flown with Mo, is asked to renew Mo's 90-day solo endorsement without flying with him. What does §61.87(p) require?
notes.back: A) She may authorise solo only after training Mo in that make and model and finding him proficient
notes.choices:
A) She may authorise solo only after training Mo in that make and model and finding him proficient
B) She may sign if the logbook shows his earlier endorsements
C) She may sign if he passed the pre-solo test within 90 days
D) She may sign: any instructor may update a solo endorsement
notes.choicesExplained: D: §61.87(p) lets an authorized instructor update the endorsement every 90 days, but an update authorises solo, so she must first train Mo and find him proficient. B: earlier endorsements do not show his current proficiency. C: the pre-solo test does not replace her own training and findings.
notes.explanation: Whoever authorises solo, including a 90-day update, must have trained the student in that make and model, because AC 61-65K's A.7 update certifies both the training and his proficiency.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.87 Solo requirements for student pilots (eCFR), paragraph (p)
notes.evidence: No instructor may authorize a student pilot to perform a solo flight unless that instructor has— (1) Given that student pilot training in the make and model of aircraft or a similar make and model of aircraft in which the solo flight is to be flown;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Within what distance may an endorsed student fly solo to another airport to practise takeoffs and landings?
notes.back: 25 nautical miles from the airport where the student normally trains.
notes.explanation: The purpose of such a flight must be to practise takeoffs and landings at that other airport.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)
notes.evidence: (1) Solo flights may be made to another airport that is within 25 nautical miles from the airport where the student pilot normally receives training, provided—
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What training must precede solo practice at another airport within 25 NM?
notes.back: Instructor flight training at that airport: both directions over the route, pattern entry and exit, and takeoffs and landings there.
notes.explanation: The instructor who gave this training then endorses the logbook for the flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (b)(1)
notes.evidence: (i) An authorized instructor has given the student pilot flight training at the other airport, and that training includes flight in both directions over the route, entering and exiting the traffic pattern, and takeoffs and landings at the other airport;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Amir, endorsed for solo, wants to practise landings alone at an airport 30 NM from his home field, where he has flown with his instructor. Does the 25 NM provision of §61.93(b)(1) cover this?
notes.back: No: beyond 25 NM from where the flight originated, the solo cross-country requirements of §61.93 apply.
notes.explanation: The 25 NM provision is an exception for nearby airports; a flight further out is treated like a solo cross-country.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (a)(1)
notes.evidence: (i) Conducting a solo cross-country flight, or any flight greater than 25 nautical miles from the airport from where the flight originated.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Within what distance may a student make repeated solo cross-country flights over one trained route without a separate endorsement for each flight?
notes.back: 50 nautical miles from the airport where the flight originated.
notes.explanation: The student still needs the solo and solo cross-country endorsements; only the per-flight endorsements are dropped.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (b)(2)
notes.evidence: for repeated solo cross country flights to another airport within 50 nautical miles from which the flight originated, separate endorsements are not required to be made for each flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Sofia holds solo and solo cross-country endorsements and an endorsement for repeated solo flights between her home field and an airport 38 NM away, a route she flew both ways with her instructor. Today she will fly it again. What further endorsement does today's flight need?
notes.back: B) None specific to today: the repeated-flight endorsement covers it
notes.choices:
A) A new endorsement reviewing today's planning
B) None specific to today: the repeated-flight endorsement covers it
C) A Class B airspace endorsement
D) A new pre-solo knowledge test
notes.choicesExplained: A: the per-flight planning endorsement is what the 50 NM provision removes. C: nothing suggests Class B airspace. D: the pre-solo test is a one-off step before first solo.
notes.explanation: Within 50 NM, over the trained route, separate endorsements are not required for each flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (b)(2)
notes.evidence: for repeated solo cross country flights to another airport within 50 nautical miles from which the flight originated, separate endorsements are not required to be made for each flight.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which solo cross-country endorsement must come from the instructor who conducted the training?
notes.back: The endorsement for the specific category of aircraft to be flown.
notes.explanation: A second standing endorsement covers the make and model.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(1)
notes.evidence: (1) A student pilot must have a solo cross-country endorsement from the authorized instructor who conducted the training that is placed in that person's logbook for the specific category of aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Besides the category endorsement, what standing solo cross-country endorsement does a student need?
notes.back: One from an authorized instructor for the specific make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: Unlike the category endorsement, the rule does not say it must come from the instructor who conducted the training.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(2)
notes.evidence: (2) A student pilot must have a solo cross-country endorsement from an authorized instructor that is placed in that person's logbook for the specific make and model of aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the endorsement made for each solo cross-country flight state?
notes.back: The make and model; that planning is correct and the student is prepared to fly safely under known conditions; that instructor limitations are met.
notes.explanation: It is written after the instructor has reviewed that flight's planning.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(3)
notes.evidence: (i) Specify the make and model of aircraft to be flown; (ii) State that the student's preflight planning and preparation is correct and that the student is prepared to make the flight safely under the known conditions; and (iii) State that any limitations required by the student's authorized instructor are met.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Nia holds standing solo cross-country endorsements for the airplane category and for her trainer's make and model. Tomorrow she flies a new cross-country route. What else must be in her logbook?
notes.back: An endorsement for that flight, made by an instructor after reviewing her cross-country planning.
notes.explanation: The standing endorsements do not cover an individual flight; each cross-country needs its own planning review and endorsement.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (c)(3)
notes.evidence: (3) For each cross-country flight, the authorized instructor who reviews the cross-country planning must make an endorsement in the person's logbook after reviewing that person's cross-country planning
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Must the each-flight solo cross-country endorsement come from the student's usual instructor?
notes.back: No, but whoever makes it must ensure all other required endorsements are already in place.
notes.explanation: AC 61-65K gives the category and make-and-model endorsements as examples of what must already be there.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 20.6, page 12
notes.evidence: This endorsement does not need to be made by the instructor who normally provides training to the student. However, the flight instructor must ensure that all other required endorsements have been previously provided
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor have determined about a student's planning before permitting a solo cross-country?
notes.back: That the cross-country planning is correct for the flight.
notes.explanation: It is the first of five findings §61.93(d) requires before the flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (1) Determined that the student's cross-country planning is correct for the flight;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What weather check must the instructor make before permitting a solo cross-country?
notes.back: Review current and forecast weather and determine the flight can be completed under VFR.
notes.explanation: The forecast matters as well as current weather, because the whole flight must be completable under VFR.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (2) Reviewed the current and forecast weather conditions and has determined that the flight can be completed under VFR;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor determine about the student's ability before permitting a solo cross-country?
notes.back: That the student is proficient to conduct the flight safely.
notes.explanation: Correct planning alone is not enough; the instructor must also judge the student's proficiency for this flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (3) Determined that the student is proficient to conduct the flight safely;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which cross-country endorsement must the instructor confirm the student holds before a solo cross-country?
notes.back: The solo cross-country endorsement for the make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: The instructor checks the standing endorsements before adding the one for this flight.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (4) Determined that the student has the appropriate solo cross-country endorsement for the make and model of aircraft to be flown; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor confirm about the student's solo endorsement before a solo cross-country?
notes.back: That it is current for the make and model to be flown.
notes.explanation: A solo endorsement older than 90 days would fail this check.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (5) Determined that the student's solo flight endorsement is current for the make and model aircraft to be flown.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A student brings a correct plan for a solo cross-country, but the forecast shows the destination going below VFR minimums before her arrival time. What must the instructor do?
notes.back: C) Not permit the flight: the instructor must determine it can be completed under VFR
notes.choices:
A) Endorse the flight and note the weather
B) Endorse it if she files a flight plan
C) Not permit the flight: the instructor must determine it can be completed under VFR
D) Endorse it if she holds a night solo endorsement
notes.choicesExplained: A: noting the weather does not meet the requirement to find the flight can be completed under VFR. B and D: neither changes the forecast.
notes.explanation: The weather finding looks at the forecast, and here the forecast rules out completing the flight under VFR.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.93 Solo cross-country flight requirements (eCFR), paragraph (d)
notes.evidence: (2) Reviewed the current and forecast weather conditions and has determined that the flight can be completed under VFR;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What training must precede a student's solo flight in Class B airspace?
notes.back: Ground and flight training from an authorized instructor on that Class B area, with the flight training in that specific area.
notes.explanation: Training in some other Class B area does not count.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.95 Operations in Class B airspace and at airports located within Class B airspace (eCFR), paragraph (a)
notes.evidence: (1) The student pilot has received both ground and flight training from an authorized instructor on that Class B airspace area, and the flight training was received in the specific Class B airspace area for which solo flight is authorized;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How recent must a student's Class B solo endorsement be, and who must give it?
notes.back: Dated within the 90 days before the flight, by the authorized instructor who gave the flight training.
notes.explanation: The endorsement must also say the student was found proficient for solo in that specific Class B area.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.95 Operations in Class B airspace and at airports located within Class B airspace (eCFR), paragraph (a)
notes.evidence: (2) The logbook of that student pilot has been endorsed by the authorized instructor who gave the student pilot flight training, and the endorsement is dated within the 90-day period preceding the date of the flight in that Class B airspace area; and
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the endorsement for student solo at an airport within Class B airspace specify?
notes.back: That the student received the required ground and flight training and is proficient for solo operations at that specific airport.
notes.explanation: The training behind it must have been received at that airport, and the endorsement is dated within 90 days.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.95 Operations in Class B airspace and at airports located within Class B airspace (eCFR), paragraph (b)
notes.evidence: (3) The logbook endorsement specifies that the student pilot has received the required ground and flight training, and has been found proficient to conduct solo flight operations at that specific airport.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Ella holds a current endorsement for solo in the Class B airspace over her training area. She now wants to land solo at an airport inside that Class B where student solo operations are allowed. What else does she need?
notes.back: A) Ground and flight training at that airport and an endorsement for solo operations there
notes.choices:
A) Ground and flight training at that airport and an endorsement for solo operations there
B) A new student pilot certificate
C) Only a clearance from air traffic control
D) Nothing: the airspace endorsement covers its airports
notes.choicesExplained: D: paragraph (b) sets separate conditions for airports within Class B. B: the certificate is not the missing item. C: a clearance does not replace the training and endorsement.
notes.explanation: §61.95 treats solo in the Class B area and solo at an airport within it as separate authorisations.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.95 Operations in Class B airspace and at airports located within Class B airspace (eCFR), paragraph (b)
notes.evidence: (1) The student pilot has received both ground and flight training from an instructor authorized to provide training to operate at that airport, and the flight and ground training has been received at the specific airport for which the solo flight is authorized;
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: In what may a person log training time received from an authorized instructor?
notes.back: An aircraft, full flight simulator, flight training device or aviation training device.
notes.explanation: Training in any of these devices can be logged, as long as an authorized instructor gave it.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.51 Pilot logbooks (eCFR), paragraph (h)
notes.evidence: (1) A person may log training time when that person receives training from an authorized instructor in an aircraft, full flight simulator, flight training device, or aviation training device.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must an instructor's training-time entry in a logbook include?
notes.back: A description of the training, the lesson length, and the instructor's signature, certificate number and expiration or recent experience end date.
notes.explanation: The entry must also be legible.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.51 Pilot logbooks (eCFR), paragraph (h)(2)
notes.evidence: (ii) Include a description of the training given, the length of the training lesson, and the authorized instructor's signature, certificate number, and certificate expiration date or recent experience end date, consistent with the requirements of § 61.197.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: According to AC 61-65K, what must every endorsement include?
notes.back: Legibility; the instructor's signature, date and certificate number; and the recent experience end date or certificate expiration date.
notes.explanation: The printed name is optional under the same guidance.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, Sample Endorsements, page A-7
notes.evidence: Each endorsement must be legible and include the instructor’s signature, date of signature, certificated flight instructor (CFI) or certificated ground instructor certificate number, and flight instructor recent experience (RE) end date or certificate expiration date, as applicable.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: An instructor whose certificate was issued in 2025 signs a learner's training entry. Which date does she write beside her certificate number?
notes.back: Her recent experience end date, as her certificate has no expiration date.
notes.explanation: The rule asks for the expiration date or the recent experience end date, whichever applies to the certificate.
notes.source: 14 CFR § 61.51 Pilot logbooks (eCFR), paragraph (h)(2)
notes.evidence: the authorized instructor's signature, certificate number, and certificate expiration date or recent experience end date, consistent with the requirements of § 61.197.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What does an instructor's endorsement certify when used to show ground training for a knowledge test?
notes.back: That the applicant satisfactorily completed the ground training for the certificate or rating and is prepared for the test.
notes.explanation: It is one of several accepted ways to show ground-school or home-study completion.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 10.2, page 3
notes.evidence: An endorsement from an authorized instructor who has certified that the applicant has satisfactorily completed the ground training required for the certificate or rating sought and is prepared for the test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: A learner prepared for the private pilot knowledge test with a home-study course he compiled himself, and has no graduation certificate. What should the instructor do before endorsing him?
notes.back: Review the course materials and question him to confirm he completed it and has the required knowledge.
notes.explanation: AC 61-65K describes this route for applicants who cannot show any of the other accepted documents.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 10.2, page 4
notes.evidence: The instructor will review the course materials and question the applicant to determine that the course was completed and that the applicant does possess the knowledge required for the certificate or rating sought. The instructor will then complete an endorsement certifying that the applicant is prepared for the knowledge test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: For which knowledge test can the home-study curriculum review endorsement not be used?
notes.back: The airline transport pilot airplane multiengine knowledge test.
notes.explanation: Applicants for that test must instead present a graduation certificate showing they completed the airline transport pilot Certification Training Program.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.86, page A-23
notes.evidence: Note: This endorsement cannot be used for the ATP Airplane Multiengine Knowledge Test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What does the §61.39(a)(6)(i)–(ii) practical test prerequisites endorsement certify?
notes.back: Training received and logged within the 2 calendar months before the month of application, and readiness for the practical test.
notes.explanation: Its window counts calendar months back from the month of application.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.1, page A-7
notes.evidence: has received and logged training time within 2 calendar months preceding the month of application in preparation for the practical test and they are prepared for the required practical test
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Does the certificate-specific practical test endorsement replace the §61.39 prerequisites endorsements?
notes.back: No: it is required in addition to them.
notes.explanation: An applicant for a private pilot practical test therefore carries both kinds of endorsement.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.37, page A-14
notes.evidence: The endorsement for a practical test is required in addition to the 14 CFR § 61.39 endorsements provided in paragraphs A.1 and A.2.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Hana's last logged training was in March. She applies for her practical test in June. Can her instructor sign the prerequisites endorsement as worded in AC 61-65K?
notes.back: C) No: training must be logged within the 2 calendar months before June
notes.choices:
A) Yes: training within 90 days is enough
B) Yes: her knowledge test report covers it
C) No: training must be logged within the 2 calendar months before June
D) No: training must be within 30 days of the test
notes.choicesExplained: A: the window is 2 calendar months, not 90 days. B: the knowledge test report does not stand in for logged training. D: no 30-day rule appears in the endorsement.
notes.explanation: The 2 calendar months before June are April and May, so March training falls outside.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.1, page A-7
notes.evidence: has received and logged training time within 2 calendar months preceding the month of application in preparation for the practical test
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What does the knowledge-test deficiencies endorsement certify?
notes.back: That the applicant has shown satisfactory knowledge of the subject areas missed on the airman knowledge test.
notes.explanation: It is the second of the two §61.39 prerequisite endorsements, alongside the recent-training one.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.2, page A-7
notes.evidence: I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has demonstrated satisfactory knowledge of the subject areas in which they were deficient on the [applicable] airman knowledge test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: An applicant scored 85% on the knowledge test and missed questions on weather services. What must the instructor certify before the practical test?
notes.back: That the applicant now shows satisfactory knowledge of the weather-services areas missed on the test.
notes.explanation: The endorsement is about the specific areas the knowledge test found deficient.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.2, page A-7
notes.evidence: has demonstrated satisfactory knowledge of the subject areas in which they were deficient on the [applicable] airman knowledge test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Where may an instructor write the retest endorsement after a failed knowledge test?
notes.back: In the space at the bottom of the applicant's Airman Knowledge Test Report (AKTR).
notes.explanation: The endorsement certifies the additional training §61.49 requires before a retest.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.77, page A-21
notes.evidence: In the case of a failed knowledge test, the instructor may complete the endorsement in the space provided at the bottom of the applicant’s Airman Knowledge Test Report (AKTR).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What must the instructor sign for each retake of a practical test?
notes.back: The instructor's recommendation block on the reverse of FAA Form 8710-1.
notes.explanation: The signature is needed for each retake, not only the first one.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.77, page A-21
notes.evidence: The instructor must sign the block provided for the instructor’s recommendation on the reverse side of FAA Form 8710-1, Airman Certificate and/or Rating Application, for each retake of a practical test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Leo failed the commercial pilot knowledge test last week. After extra ground training, what lets him retest?
notes.back: A) The instructor's §61.49 retest endorsement, which may be written on his AKTR
notes.choices:
A) The instructor's §61.49 retest endorsement, which may be written on his AKTR
B) A new medical certificate
C) An examiner's signature on FAA Form 8710-1
D) Nothing: he simply books another test
notes.choicesExplained: D: a retest follows additional training that an instructor certifies. B: a medical certificate is unrelated to test authorisation. C: the Form 8710-1 recommendation is for practical test retakes, signed by the instructor.
notes.explanation: The sample retest endorsement certifies the additional training §61.49 requires.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.77, page A-21
notes.evidence: I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the additional [flight and/or ground, as appropriate] training as required by 14 CFR § 61.49. I have determined that they are proficient to pass the [name of] knowledge/practical test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What does the sample endorsement for the Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test (A.45) certify?
notes.back: That the applicant received the §61.185(a)(1) fundamentals of instruction training and is prepared for the test.
notes.explanation: It is the endorsement §61.183(d) requires, and the Testing Matrix accepts it as authorisation for the test.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.45, page A-15
notes.evidence: has received the required fundamentals of instruction training of 14 CFR § 61.185(a)(1). I have determined that they are prepared for the Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Jamal, a commercial pilot, has finished his fundamentals-of-instructing ground training and wants to book the Fundamentals of Instructing test. What should his instructor write in his logbook?
notes.back: C) The A.45 Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test endorsement
notes.choices:
A) The A.47 flight instructor practical test endorsement
B) The A.49 spin training endorsement
C) The A.45 Fundamentals of Instructing knowledge test endorsement
D) Nothing: instructor knowledge tests need no endorsement
notes.choicesExplained: A: A.47 is for the practical test. B: A.49 records spin training. D: since 1 September 2024 the Testing Matrix requires authorisation for this test.
notes.explanation: A.45 certifies the §61.185(a)(1) training and readiness for that knowledge test.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.45, page A-15
notes.evidence: A.45 Fundamentals of instructing knowledge test: 14 CFR § 61.183(d). I certify that [First name, MI, Last name] has received the required fundamentals of instruction training of 14 CFR § 61.185(a)(1).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: According to AC 61-65K, which flight instructor applicants need the spin training endorsement (A.49)?
notes.back: Only flight instructor airplane and flight instructor glider applicants.
notes.explanation: The endorsement states competence and instructional proficiency in stall awareness, spin entry, spins and spin recovery.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.49, page A-16
notes.evidence: The spin training endorsement is only required of flight instructor airplane and flight instructor glider applicants.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Must an instructor make a logbook entry after an unsatisfactory flight review?
notes.back: No: no entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance is required.
notes.explanation: Only a satisfactory review is endorsed, with the pilot's name, certificate grade and number, and the date.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.69, page A-20
notes.evidence: Completion of a flight review: 14 CFR § 61.56(a) and (c). No logbook entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance on a flight review is required.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: After an hour of flying, an instructor finds a pilot's flight review unsatisfactory. What must go in the pilot's logbook about the review?
notes.back: C) Nothing reflecting the unsatisfactory performance is required
notes.choices:
A) The satisfactory endorsement with a note of the weak areas
B) An entry stating the review was failed
C) Nothing reflecting the unsatisfactory performance is required
D) A report to the FAA within 10 days
notes.choicesExplained: B: the advisory circular says no such entry is required. A: a satisfactory endorsement would be false. D: no reporting duty appears in the guidance.
notes.explanation: The sample endorsement exists only for a satisfactorily completed review.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.69, page A-20
notes.evidence: No logbook entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance on a flight review is required.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Is a logbook entry required for an unsatisfactory instrument proficiency check?
notes.back: No: as with the flight review, no entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance is required.
notes.explanation: A satisfactory check is endorsed with the make and model of aircraft used and the date.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.71, page A-20
notes.evidence: No logbook entry reflecting unsatisfactory performance on an IPC is required.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What does the complex airplane endorsement (A.72) say the instructor has determined?
notes.back: That the pilot is proficient in the operation and systems of a complex airplane.
notes.explanation: It records the §61.31(e) training in a named make and model of complex airplane.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.72, page A-20
notes.evidence: has received the required training of 14 CFR § 61.31(e) in a [M/M] complex airplane. I have determined that they are proficient in the operation and systems of a complex airplane.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Under which part of §61.31 is the high-performance airplane endorsement (A.73) given?
notes.explanation: The complex endorsement is §61.31(e) and the pressurised one §61.31(g); each needs its own training.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.73, page A-21
notes.evidence: A.73 To act as PIC in a high-performance airplane: 14 CFR § 61.31(f).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: What kind of aircraft does the §61.31(g) endorsement (A.74) cover?
notes.back: A pressurised aircraft capable of high-altitude operations.
notes.explanation: It certifies proficiency in the operation and systems of a pressurised aircraft.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.74, page A-21
notes.evidence: To act as PIC in a pressurized aircraft capable of high-altitude operations: 14 CFR § 61.31(g).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Who may give the tailwheel endorsement (A.75)?
notes.back: A sport pilot instructor in a sport pilot aircraft, or a flight instructor with another rating in an airplane.
notes.explanation: Unlike the complex and high-performance endorsements, its wording speaks of proficiency in operation only, not systems.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.75, page A-21
notes.evidence: This endorsement may be given in a sport pilot aircraft by a sport pilot instructor or in an airplane by a flight instructor with a rating other than a sport pilot rating.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Grace moves up to a 180-horsepower airplane with retractable gear, flaps and a controllable-pitch propeller. Which AC 61-65K sample endorsement does her instructor give?
notes.back: B) A.72, to act as PIC in a complex airplane
notes.choices:
A) A.73, high-performance airplane
B) A.72, to act as PIC in a complex airplane
C) A.75, tailwheel airplane
D) A.74, pressurised aircraft
notes.choicesExplained: A: high performance means more than 200 horsepower. C: nothing says the airplane has a tailwheel. D: nothing says it is pressurised.
notes.explanation: The airplane fits the complex airplane definition and is not above 200 horsepower, so A.72 is the endorsement that applies.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.72, page A-20
notes.evidence: A.72 To act as PIC in a complex airplane: 14 CFR § 61.31(e).
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Does a plastic student pilot certificate expire?
notes.back: No, but some endorsements that authorise and limit a student's privileges are valid for only 90 calendar days.
notes.explanation: So a valid certificate does not by itself show that a student may fly solo.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, paragraph 20.1, page 11
notes.evidence: A new student pilot certificate issued on a plastic card does not have an expiration date. However, some of the endorsements that authorize and limit a student pilot’s privileges are valid for 90 calendar days from the date of endorsement.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: How may a flight instructor meet the TSA's recommended U.S. citizenship check for a student?
notes.back: Keep copies of the proof-of-citizenship documents for 5 years, or make the citizenship endorsement in the student's and the instructor's records.
notes.explanation: The endorsement names the document presented, such as a U.S. birth certificate or passport.
notes.source: AC 61-65K, Certification: Pilots and Flight and Ground Instructors, Appendix A, A.14, page A-9
notes.evidence: The flight instructor must keep a copy of the documents used to provide proof of citizenship for 5 years or make the following endorsement in the student’s logbook and the instructor’s logbook or other record used to record flight student endorsements
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: Which endorsement risk does the flight instructor Airman Certification Standards single out in Task II.K?
notes.back: Endorsements without appropriate limitations or expiration dates.
notes.explanation: The same task asks the applicant to prepare entries for at least two endorsement events.
notes.source: Flight Instructor for Airplane Category ACS (FAA-S-ACS-25), Area of Operation II, Task K, page 17
notes.evidence: Endorsements without appropriate limitations or expiration dates.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force

notes.front: An instructor writes 'proficient to make solo flights' for a student who struggles with crosswinds, naming no aircraft and adding no wind limit. Which Task II.K risk does this show?
notes.back: An endorsement without appropriate limitations or expiration dates.
notes.explanation: The rules let instructors list limitations needed for safety, and the solo endorsement must name a make and model.
notes.source: Flight Instructor for Airplane Category ACS (FAA-S-ACS-25), Area of Operation II, Task K, page 17
notes.evidence: Endorsements without appropriate limitations or expiration dates.
notes.validAsOf: 2026-09-26 · FAA-S-ACS-25 and 14 CFR as in force
